chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Safwan from 'Abdullah from al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said: A woman received news of her husband's death after a year or thereabouts. He said: If she is pregnant, her waiting period is until she gives birth to her child. And if she is not pregnant, her waiting period has passed if evidence is established for her that he died on such and such a day. And if she has no evidence, let her observe the waiting period from the day she heard. These two reports came as anomalous, contradicting all the hadiths. The detail contained in the latter report is also contradicted by the former report mentioned from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, because he said: She observes the waiting period from the day it reaches her, whether evidence is established for her or not. So it is permissible to depart from the numerous reports to these two reports, on the assumption that the narrator may have erred and heard the ruling of the divorced woman and thought it was the ruling of the one whose husband died, because the detail contained in the latter report and the consideration of the establishment of evidence and the completion of the waiting period upon childbirth and all that else is considered in it. And on this basis, the reports do not contradict each other. And it has been narrated that if the distance is close, it is permissible for her to marry from the day the man dies. That was narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman whose husband dies while he is absent?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi analyzes the apparent contradiction in reports regarding the 'iddah of a woman whose husband dies in absentia, noting that while some narrations suggest waiting for proof of death, the majority view holds that the period begins upon receiving news. He reconciles these by attributing discrepancies to potential narrator error (wahm) or distinguishing between cases where evidence is presented versus those where it is not, thereby preserving the consistency of the hadith corpus.
